description: `DocAccess` and the boundaries above it catch `Forbidden`, `Unauthorized` and `RpcClientError`. `GetDoc` can also fail with `DocNotFound`, so the read is `Doc | Unhandled<DocNotFound>`: there's no `title` to read until `Boundary.isUnhandled` has ruled the failure out.

errors.message:
Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Unhandled<DocNotFound> | { readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }'.
  Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Unhandled<DocNotFound>'.

title: No plain data until every error is handled

description: Read through `Session`, a doc can still fail with `Forbidden` or `DocNotFound`: both come back as the `Unhandled`'s error. Forgetting one is a type error that names it.

errors.message:
Argument of type '{ DocNotFound: () => string; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'ValueTagHandlers<DocNotFound | Forbidden> & {}'.
  Property 'Forbidden' is missing in type '{ DocNotFound: () => string; }' but required in type 'ValueTagHandlers<DocNotFound | Forbidden>'.

title: What's left must be matched exhaustively

description: Under `DocAccess`, what's left is `DocNotFound` and nothing else. An `Unauthorized` can't reach this component (`Session` caught it), so a case for it is a type error, not dead code.

errors.message: Type '() => string' is not assignable to type 'never'.

title: You can't handle an error a boundary already caught

description: `Session` already catches `Unauthorized`, so a boundary inside it that lists `"Unauthorized"` again would never see one.

errors.message:
Type '["Unauthorized"]' is not assignable to type 'readonly ["Unauthorized"] & { readonly AlreadyHandledAbove: "Unauthorized"; }'.
  Property 'AlreadyHandledAbove' is missing in type '["Unauthorized"]' but required in type '{ readonly AlreadyHandledAbove: "Unauthorized"; }'.

title: A boundary can't catch what one above it catches

description: `Boundary.useRun(DocAccess)` runs an Effect with the client's services, and resolves with what a read through `DocAccess` would return: `RenameDoc` can also fail with `DocNotFound` and `EmptyTitle`, so the result is `Doc | Unhandled<DocNotFound | EmptyTitle>`.

errors.message:
Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Unhandled<DocNotFound | EmptyTitle> | { readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }'.
  Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Unhandled<DocNotFound | EmptyTitle>'.

title: An action's errors are checked the same way

description: The client is built from the RPC client's layer. An Effect that needs another service (`Analytics` here) can't be run under any boundary of that client.

title: An Effect can only use services the client provides

description: A boundary that catches `DocNotFound` too leaves nothing, so its hook returns the doc itself: no `Unhandled`, nothing to check. `useSession` on the doc list is the same: `Session` and the boundaries above it catch everything `ListDocs` can fail with. This file compiles.
title: Once every error is caught, there is no failure to get

description: The root declares `AppError`, everything a `DocsClient` call can fail with. A boundary can only list tags of it, so a typo is caught, with a suggestion.

errors.message: Type '"DocNotFund"' is not assignable to type '"DocNotFound" | "EmptyTitle" | "Forbidden" | "RpcClientError" | "Unauthorized"'. Did you mean '"DocNotFound"'?

title: Tags come from the errors the root declares

description: Boundaries match failures by tag. Add a second error tagged `"Forbidden"` to the universe, and a boundary that catches `"Forbidden"` can't say which one its fallback gets, so it doesn't type-check.

errors.message:
Type '["Forbidden"]' is not assignable to type 'readonly ["Forbidden"] & { readonly TagSharedByMoreThanOneError: "Forbidden"; }'.
  Property 'TagSharedByMoreThanOneError' is missing in type '["Forbidden"]' but required in type '{ readonly TagSharedByMoreThanOneError: "Forbidden"; }'.

title: A tag must name one error

description: `DocAccess`'s fallback gets the universe's `Forbidden`, with a `docId`. A query that fails with another `"Forbidden"` (an `orgId`, no `docId`) can't be read through it: its failure would reach a fallback that reads `docId`.
